title: Writing mathematics in the age of AI
author_line: Martin Hairer Professor of Pure Mathematics at EPFL and Imperial College London
summary: Hairer proposes concrete best practices for writing mathematics papers produced with AI help: scrutinise AI arguments adversarially, disclose meaningful AI contributions specifically, track down attribution of ideas, and never paste AI output directly into papers.

understanding_evidence: the most dangerous trap that a mathematician risks falling into is to use an argument provided by an AI system without fully understanding it
institutions_evidence: we, as a community, are still in the process of figuring out what should and shouldn’t be considered best practice
adoption_evidence: I believe that positions are defensible in good faith
overall_evidence: This post should not be construed as any opinion regarding the ethics of AI usage, whether in mathematical research or otherwise.

title: Why do mathematics in the age of AI
author_line: Srivatsav Kunnawalkam Elayavalli , Assistant Professor, UC Berkeley
summary: Drawing on the Carnatic concepts of manōdharma and bhāva, the author argues that mathematics' true value lies in personal 'aha moments' independent of AI, so even if AI surpasses humans at mathematics, mathematicians should not panic but use AI insofar as it enriches them while adapting to professional change.
capability_evidence: I completely recognize the power and beauty of AI, and am ready to accept that it probably already is ‘better’ than me at math.
understanding_evidence: the conscious inculcation of bhāva is the source and also the pinnacle of human achievement, and by design is independent of anything to do with artificial intelligence.
community_evidence: mathematics is one prominent route to travel that I believe will always exist and be available for everyone until humanity exists.
adoption_evidence: I will use them and appreciate them insofar as it invokes bhāva and enriches me.
overall_evidence: I think this is not a time for mathematicians to panic, but it is a time for us to be honest with ourselves and work to make our mathematical experience richer.
author_evidence: Srivatsav Kunnawalkam Elayavalli , Assistant Professor, UC Berkeley
